summary: Email platform unifying marketing, lifecycle, and transactional messages for software companies.
editor_note: The sharper bet is one contact model, visual system, and automation layer for every lifecycle message rather than a product-email ESP beside a marketing suite. The product shows branching workflows, goal conversions, themes, APIs, SDKs, and agent controls; paid plans start at $49 monthly. Revision-safe agent writes and dashboard review preserve a useful human boundary. The open question is whether this breadth can grow without recreating the bloat Loops is replacing.
investors: Craft Ventures, Alt Capital, SV Angel, Liquid 2, Soma Capital, BoxGroup, Twenty Two Ventures, Y Combinator

sources.label: Loops Workflows API and agent-safety update
Loops public launch and funding announcement

product_evidence.claim: The official homepage combines marketing, product, and transactional lifecycle email with branching workflows, shared themes, dynamic segments, goal conversion reporting, APIs, SDKs, and sender-reputation controls.

The official agent surface exposes MCP, skills, a CLI, SDKs, and APIs for contacts, events, campaigns, transactional messages, email content, and workflows; campaigns are drafted through the API and reviewed and sent from the dashboard.
The pricing page includes every feature on a free plan for up to 1,000 contacts and 4,000 rolling 30-day sends, while the first paid contact tier starts at $49 per month with unlimited sends.

The August 2026 product update adds a Workflows API, an official Claude connector, conditional sections, and revision-bound writes that reject stale workflow updates instead of overwriting newer work.
The company launch announcement describes a no-code email automation product designed for both developers and non-developers, alongside the disclosed $3.2M financing.
Y Combinator lists Loops as an active Winter 2022 company founded in 2022, with a team of 10 in Washington, DC, building email sending for software companies.

market_context.primary_user: Product, marketing, and engineering teams at software companies that currently split lifecycle email across several tools.
market_context.differentiation: Loops puts campaigns, behavior-triggered workflows, and transactional delivery on one contact model and visual system, then exposes controlled creation and maintenance through agent-ready APIs.
market_context.why_now: Its 2026 workflow and agent interfaces move the product beyond a lighter email editor toward a shared lifecycle control plane while retaining draft, review, and revision checks around higher-risk changes.

risks.claim: Agent access expands the operational blast radius of incorrect contact, content, workflow, or send actions even when stale workflow writes are rejected.
risks.basis: The agent page exposes writes across contacts, events, content, workflows, campaigns, and transactional email; the changelog only documents stale-write protection for workflows.

risks.claim: Adding campaigns, transactional delivery, visual systems, analytics, workflows, integrations, and agent controls could eventually recreate the complexity the product is positioned to remove.
risks.basis: VentureDex editorial assessment based on the breadth visible across the official homepage, agent surface, and product changelog.

risks.claim: The financing is verified, but calling it Seed would turn a third-party database convention into a source claim that neither the company announcement nor the original dated report makes.
risks.basis: Both financing sources name the $3.2M amount and Craft Ventures as lead without assigning a round stage.

unnamed_round_assessment.reason: Loops and the original dated report both confirm the $3.2M financing and Craft Ventures lead, but neither names the round. VentureDex therefore preserves it as Unspecified rather than inferring Seed from database labels; company and product identity are cross-checked against the official site and Y Combinator profile.
